name: Read me
rows: Revised radiopharmaceutical model integrating the Nouran Zaid draft, Nicolas Karakatsanis blueprint and the supplied IDRP document.
Nodes defines record identity; Elements defines node properties; Links defines relationships; Profiles defines conditional context; Common metadata applies to all new nodes.
23 new nodes and optional additions to six existing nodes; all 29 MIDRC baseline nodes remain. The complete model has 90 nodes.
Proposed operational definitions. LOINC/RadLex/NucLex and regulatory mappings require separate release-specific review.
See each quantity definition and profile. Identifiers are strings. Missing values are not zero. No source example is a clinical default.
Radiopharmaceutical_Revisions_and_Rationale_v0.4.0.xlsx maps each source entry and explains the change.

Nicolas A Karakatsanis, Atlas Haddadi Avval, Julia Brosch-Lenz, Irene Buvat, Abhinav Jha, Mario Jreige, Quanzheng Li, Neeta Pandit-Taskar, Babak Saboury, Jazmin Schwartz, Nouran Zaid, Tahir I Yusufaly, Tyler J Bradshaw
No institutional adoption, live Gen3 deployment or clinical validation is claimed. All patient examples are invented.

name: Nodes
rows: One biological target identity; expression, binding and internalization are contextual evidence records.
One versioned computational model specification, independent of any execution or prediction.
One decay branch or one emission component with a specified energy definition and yield.
One patient-specific dispensing event allocating a traceable physical unit to a prescription.
One reviewed external identifier assignment to one explicitly typed entity; schema-level ontology mappings remain semantic_mapping records.
One physical lot of a precursor, radionuclide stock or other manufacturing material.
One versioned commercial or investigational medicinal-product formulation, distinct from agent, authorization and batch.
One parameter value or distribution for a model specification or execution, with units and provenance.
One simulated or predicted result from a model execution; separate from a measured dose or outcome.
One recorded execution of a computational model with explicit inputs and information cutoff.
One chemically specified substance or molecular component, independent of commercial packaging.
One containment relationship between two package specifications.
One actual production, compounding, reconstitution or dilution event with specified inputs and output batch.
One ingredient role and quantity specification in a medicinal-product formulation.
One versioned package specification for a medicinal product, not a physical vial.
One nuclide identity and versioned physical reference description, including stable daughters.
One reference agent in the v0.4 profile. Existing product-like records remain readable; migrate them explicitly rather than silently reinterpreting their identifiers.
One physical manufacturing batch; one or more timed QC results are linked through radiopharmaceutical_test.
One procurement request or patient-specific prescription, explicitly distinguished by order_kind.
One nonpatient QC, biological-reference or computational-evaluation result with an explicit subject and method.
One physical vial, syringe or other traceable unit from a batch at a stated calibration time.
One citable evidence context, population or experimental dataset; not an individual patient observation.
One product-specific regulatory application or authorization state in one jurisdiction at a stated date.
One dated commercial supply presentation or catalog offer; not a clinical prescription.
One evidence-supported proposed pairing of diagnostic and therapeutic agents; not an assertion of interchangeable kinetics.
One adverse-event episode or graded assessment

name: Profiles
rows: Human diagnosis, treatment and follow-up with optional product-to-administration traceability.

name: Common metadata
rows: Stable submitter-assigned identifier, unique within a project. Do not encode direct patient identifiers.

A 128-bit identifier. Depending on the mechanism used to generate it, it is either guaranteed to be different from all other UUIDs/GUIDs generated until 3400 AD or extremely likely to be different. Its relatively small size lends itself well to sorting, ordering, and hashing of all sorts, storing in databases, simple allocation, and ease of programming in general.
